title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: O(1)-memory Brent-cycle rho with hard cap 1.65 sqrt(r) and success 0.4215 in the reviewer's own acceptance model (claim 128.24)

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and the given T=[x]P0 in BLS12-381 G1, recover x with probability at least 0.42 using at most 2^128.235075 target-group-operation equivalents, normalized by the fixed BLS G1 addition price C=2000. METHOD: table Th[h]=[c_h]P0+[d_h]T for h=0..R-1, R=1024, built once (2048 scalar multiplications = 784384 units), every d_h nonzero mod r; a state is (X,a,b) with X=[a]P0+[b]T; the step is h=H(x(X)) (one 64-bit limb of the canonical x-coordinate, fixed odd multiplier, xor-shift, top 10 bits), X<-X+Th[h] (one group addition, the reference operation), a<-a+c_h mod r, b<-b+d_h mod r (two 4-limb modular additions). The step is a function of the group element alone, so the trajectory is a deterministic map; no history, no dictionary, no distinguished points. CYCLE DETECTION AND SOLVE: Brent's algorithm with a checkpoint pair and a hare pair, each carrying its exact exponent pair, O(1) memory; when the two points agree, [ta]P0+[tb]T=[ha]P0+[hb]T gives x=(ta-ha)*(hb-tb)^-1 mod r, which is exact because the points are equal, and is invertible with probability 1-1/r (a degenerate draw restarts inside the same cap). SO NO USELESS CYCLE EXISTS: a pair of equal points always yields x unless the exponent pairs are identical, i.e. the walk returned to the same state, and a two-step return needs 2*Th[h]=0, impossible in a group of odd prime order r; longer same-state returns are codimension-one coincidences with probability about 1/r, not a family. This is why the submission has no canonicalisation and no quotient: a +/-1 or Frobenius quotient makes the inverse of a multiplier equal its negative/conjugate and creates structured fruitless two-cycles of density 1/(2R) or 1/(12R). HARD CAP AND SUCCESS: the run is hard-capped at B=ceil(33*sqrt(r)/20)=2^128.151011 evaluations (1.65*sqrt(r)) and reports FAILURE when the cap is reached, so no branch is unbounded and no cost is an average over successful runs. The success bound is computed in the reviewer's own acceptance model (the model quoted in the rejection of 68b71f2d): with (u,v)=(mu,lam)/sqrt(N) of joint density exp(-(u+v)^2/2) on u,v>=0, a checkpoint stored at scaled position p admits u<=p AND p+lam<=end(p) with end(p)=min(next checkpoint,cap), so a schedule admits a staircase and the step budget truncates the window; the first-repeat rule used in v2 does not follow from its own cap and is withdrawn. For Brent's dyadic schedule the admitted mass is sum_j [G(p_j,V_j)-G(p_{j-1},V_j)] with V_j=max_{i>=j}(min(2*p_i,B)-p_i) and G(a,b)=int_0^a int_0^b exp(-(u+v)^2/2) dv du, swept over the dyadic phase in [1,2): at B=1.65 the worst alignment gives 0.421535, above the required 0.39. The same code reproduces the reviewer's figure G(16/15,8/15)=0.404102 at cap 1.60, and an independent Monte-Carlo of the same model gives 0.4180 with Wilson 95% [0.4112,0.4249]. COST: B=2^128.151011 evaluations at 1+120/2000=1.06 units each (one reference addition plus hash 20, two 4-limb exponent additions 40, loop and branch 20, amortized checkpoint 10, Brent comparisons 30 instructions) = 2^128.235075 units; the reference addition is charged at the organizer's fixed 2000, not its measured 2298. Additive items 784384 (table) + 1532 (start and verification, four scalar multiplications) + 64 = 785980 units = 2^19.584, i.e. 2^-108.651 of the main term. W=2^128.235075 and the claim is 3206/25=128.24, log2 W rounded up at the hundredth and reduced, checked with W^100<=2^12824 in exact integer arithmetic. Peak memory 164480 bytes (1024 point table + constant state + 64 KiB code); preprocessing is the table only, no advice, no amortization over targets, and the identity target T=O returns x=0. The single heuristic (random-mapping collision time) is disclosed and measured at toy scope: 1,200 toy trials on prime-order groups at 21 and 24 bits, under the same cap rule ceil(1.65*sqrt(q)), solved 0.428-0.445 of the time (Wilson 95% intervals [0.389,0.485], all containing the model's 0.4215 and above 0.39), with zero degenerate relations and zero bookkeeping failures.

experiments.purpose: Section A checks the production facts on BLS12-381 G1 itself with standard-library integer arithmetic: p and r prime, P0 on y^2=x^3+4, P0 not infinity, [r]P0=O, [r-1]P0=-P0, closure of affine addition and doubling on the curve, the collision identity [a1]P0+[b1]T=[a2]P0+[b2]T => x=(a1-a2)/(b2-b1) verified on real points by constructing two equal states from chosen exponents, and that sampled step-table entries [c]P0 are on the curve and of order r. Section B runs the complete declared algorithm at toy scale on a cyclic group of prime order q (safe-prime subgroup of F_p^*, p=2q+1): the same hash-derived adding walk, the same precomputed jump table, the same O(1)-memory Brent detection with checkpoint and hare exponent pairs, the same relation solve and the same verification g^x=T, under the hard cap ceil(1.65*sqrt(q)), the same rule as production. It reports the fraction of trials solved inside the cap with a Wilson 95% interval, the evaluation counts divided by sqrt(q), degenerate relations and bookkeeping failures. Section C reports the exact ledger: the cap as an exact integer, the per-step instruction ledger in units of C=2000, the additive items, the peak-memory bound and the claim m/100 with W^100<=2^m checked in integer arithmetic. Toy statistics are evidence at toy scope only; the production claim is analytic. Section D computes the success probability in the reviewer's acceptance model (joint density exp(-(u+v)^2/2), admitted set u<=p and p+lam<=end(p), staircase over the dyadic schedule, full phase sweep): it reproduces the reviewer's G(16/15,8/15)=0.404102 at cap 1.60, reports the worst alignment at the declared cap 1.65 as 0.421535, and cross-checks that mass by an independent Monte-Carlo sampler of the same model.
